definitions.short: not (the simple or abs. negation); by implication, no ; often used with other particles
definitions.usage: × before, or else, ere, except, ig(-norant), much, less, nay, neither, never, no((-ne), -r, (-thing)), (× as though...,(can-), for) not (out of), of nought, otherwise, out of, surely, as truly as, of a truth, verily, for want, whether, without.
definitions.full: H3808. lo לֹא or לוֺא adverb not (Arabic , Aramaic לָא , , Sabean לא , Ass. lâ ; not in Ethiopic: compare Kö ii. 1. 236 Walker AJSL 1896, 237 ff. ) — לוֺא , according to Masora (Fr MM 248 ), 35 t., besides בְּלוֺא 6t., and הֲלוֺא , the orthography of which varies much ( ib. p. 251 ), e.g. in Samuel always הֲלוֺא , in Chronicles always הֲלֹא , on the whole הֲלוֺא 141t., הֲלֹא 128t.; twice, according to Masora, written לו (Qr לֹא ), 1Sam 2:16 ; 20:2 , once לה Deut 3:11 Kt: — not — denying objectively, like οὐ (not μὴ = אַל ): — 1 in predication: a. with a verb ; so most frequently, and nearly always ( a ) with the finite tenses, whether perfect ( Gen 2:5 ; b 4:5 etc.) or imperfect ( 3:4 ; 8:21-22 , etc.); in short circumstantial clauses, as 44:4 הרחיקו לא , Isa 40:20 יִמּוֺט לֹא , and with a final force 41:7 ; Exod 28:32 (see Ges § 156 . 3 R. b, c Dr § 162 ). Governing two closely connected verbs (Dr § 115 , לא ) 28:43 וָמֵתוּ עָוֺן יִשְׂאוּ וְלֹא , Lev 19:12 , 29 b Deut 7:25-26 , 19:10 ; 22:1 and elsewhere; and two parallel clauses (Ges § 152 . 3) Isa 23:4 b Psa 9:19 ; 44:19 ; Job 3:1 and elsewhere With the imperfect, especially with 2 person, לֹא often expresses (not, like אַל , a deprecation, do not . . ., let not . . ., but) a prohibition , as Gen 2:17 מִמֶּנּוּ תאֹכַל לֹא thou shall not eat of it, 3:1 , 3 ; Exod 20:3 לְךָ לֹאיִֿהְיֶה there shall not be to thee, etc., 20:13 תגנב לא , etc. With the coh. and jussive moods (which are negatived regularly by אַל ), it occurs only exceptionally (Ges § 109 . 1 b R. 1), Gen 24:8 ; 1Sam 14:36 ; 2Sam 17:12 ; 18:14 ; 1Kin 2:6 ; Ezek 48:14 . ( b ) with the infinitive (which is negatived by בִּלְתִּי , q. v.), only once, in בְּלֹא ( 4a ), and with לְ , in the sense of cannot , or must not ; Judg 1:19 להורישׁ לא כי for it was not (possible) to dispossess, etc. Amos 6:10 י בשׁם ׳להזכיר לא , 1Chr 5:1 ; 15:2 (Dr § 202. 2 ); compare Aramaic לָא Dan 6:9 ; Ezra 6:8 . On its use with the participle, see b c. ( c ) לא always negates properly the word immediately following: hence, in a verbal sentence, where this is not the verb, some special stress rests upon it, Gen 32:29 וג עוֺד ׳יֵאָמֵר יַעֲקֹב לֹא not Jacob shall thy name be called any more, but Israel, 45:8 אֹתִי שְׁלַחְתֶּם אַתֶּם לֹא Not ye (in our idiom: It is not ye who) have sent me hither, but God, Exod 16:8 ; 1Sam 8:7 וג אֹתִי כִּי מָאָסוּ ׳אֹתְךָ לֹא כִּי , Psa 115:17 ; without a following correcting clause, Gen 38:9 ; Num 16:29 י ׳לֹא שְׁלָחָנִי׃ Not ׳י (but another) hath sent me, Deut 32:27 ׳י זֹאת מָּעַל לֹא , 1Chr 17:4 ; Deut 8:9 ; Isa 28:28 ֗֗֗ לנצח לא not for ever (but only for a while) . . . (so 57:16 ; Psa 9:19 ; 49:18 ; 103:9 ; but Isa 13:20 לנצח תשׁב לא is, will not be inhabited for ever), 43:22 ; Job 13:16 ; 32:9 ; hence rhetorically, insinuating something very different, not named, 2Kin 6:10 not once, and not twice (but repeatedly), Ezra 10:13 ; Jer 4:11 a wind לְהַָבר׃ וְלוֺא לְזָרוֺת לֹא not to winnow, and not to cleanse (but to exterminate), Isa 45:13 ; 48:1 b Josh 24:12 ; Dan 11:20 , 29 ; Job 34:20 בְיָד לֹא (but by a Divine agency: compare Dan 2:34 ; also Job 20:26 נֻמָּ֑ךְ לֹא אֵשׁ fire not blown upon [but kindled from heaven], Lam 4:6 ; and אין Isa 47:14 ). ( d ) standing alone: ( a ) אִםלֹֿא if not , Gen 18:21 אֵדָֽעָה׃ וְאִםלֹֿא , Genesis 29:49; 42:16 ; Job 9:24 ; 24:25 ; ( β ) הֲאִ֗֗֗םלֿא , or not , Gen 24:21 waiting to know י ׳הַהִצְלִיחַ אִםלֹֿא דַּרְכּוֺ , 27:21 ; 37:32 ; Exod 16:4 ; Num 11:23 ; Deut 8:2 ; Judg 2:22 (compare אַיִן אַיִן, אִם 2d β , δ ). In answer to a question or request, to deny, or decline, Nay , Nö: 12:5 לא ויאמר , Hag 2:12 ; אדני לא Gen 23:11 ; 42:10 ; 1Sam 1:15 +; often followed by כי , Nö for . . . = Nö but . . ., Gen 18:15 צָחָ֑קְתְּ כִּי לֹא ויאמר , 19:2 ; Josh 5:14 ; 24:21 ; 1Sam 2:16 Qr (see Dr), 10:19 ( ᵐ5 MSS), 2Sam 16:18 ; 24:24 ; 1Kin 3:22 (twice in verse) +; Job 23:6 (strangely). (compare, in deprecation, אַל .) ( e ) with an interrogative force, which however does not lie in לא as such, but (as in other cases) in the contrast with a preceding clause, or in the tone of voice (compare וְ 1 f ; Ew § 324 a Ges § 150 . 1 Dr 1Sam 11:12 ): Jonah 4:11 וג אָחוּס לֹא חַסְתָּוַ֗֗֗אֲנִי ׳אַתָּה , Job 2:10 ; 22:11 ; Exod 8:22 ; 2Kin 5:26 ; Jer 49:9 (|| Obadiah 5 הֲלוֺא ), Mal 2:15 ; Lam 3:38 ; and in passages, exegesis or text. doubtful (see Commentaries), 1Sam 20:14 ; 2Sam 23:5 (but see Bu), Hosea 10:9 (Ew We), 11:5 (Ew), Job 14:16 b (but ᵐ5 Ew Di תַעֲבֹר ), Lam 1:12 (Ew Ke), 3:36 (Ke Bä). b. with adjectives and substantive : ( a ) Gen 2:18 לְבַדֹּו הָאָדָם הֱֶיוֺת טוֺב לֹא not good is man's being alone, Exod 18:17 + often ( b ) 4:16 אָנֹכִי דְּבָרִים אִישׁ לֹא , Amos 7:14 אנכי נביא לא , Num 23:9 וִיכַזֵּב אֵל אִישׁ לֹא , Deut 17:15 (see אשׁר 2 b ) Deut 20:20 ; 32:47 ; 1Sam 15:29 ; 2Sam 18:20 הַיּוֺם אַתָּה בְּשׂרָה אִישׁ לֹא , 21:2 ; 1Kin 22:33 ; 2Kin 6:19 הדרך זִה לא , Micah 2:10 ; Isa 27:11 ; Hosea 8:6 ; אלהים לא והמה Jer 2:11 ; 16:20 ; 2Kin 19:18 ; 1Kin 19:11 (twice in verse) י ׳בָרַעַשׁ לֹא , Deut 30:12-13 , Job 15:9 ; 28:14 הִיא בִי לֹא (|| עִמָּדִי אֵין )s, Psa 74:9 ; Jer 5:10 לי ׳לוא המה , 10:16 ; Deut 32:21 בָּם אֵמוּן לֹא בָּנִים , Jer 10:14 ; Hab 1:14 ; Job 16:17 ; 38:26 בּוֺ אָדָם לֹא מִדְבָּר ; 1Kin 22:17 לָאֵלֶּה אֲדֹנִים לֹא , Jer 49:31 ; Psa 22:3 לִי דוּמִיָּה וְלֹא , Job 18:17 , 19 ; 29:12 לו עֹזֵר ולא , 30:13 ; 33:9 ; Jer 2:19 אֵלַיִךְ פַחְדָּתִי וְלֹא and (that) my terror reached not unto thee, Job 21:9 ; absolute Gen 29:7 הַמִּקְנֶה הֵאָסֵף לֹאעֵֿתִ ( Hag 1:2 ), Num 20:5 ; 2Kin 4:23 שׁבת ולא חדשׁ לא , Isa 44:9 ; Jer 5:12 הוא לוא ויאמרו , Job 9:32 ; 22:16 ; 36:26 ; 41:2 ; Prov 19:7 (si vera lectio) לֹאהֵֿמָּה אֲמָרִים מְרַדֵּף words which are not , which are nought. ( c ) with the participle לֹא is rare, a finite verb being usually preferred ( Exod 34:7 יְנַקֶּה לֹא וְנַקִּה : Ew § 320 c Dr § 162 ): 2Sam 3:34 אֲסֻרוֺת לֹא יָדֶיךָ , Ezek 4:14 ; 22:24 ; Deut 28:61 ; Psa 38:15 שֹׁמֵעַ לֹא אֲשֶׁר כְּאִישׁ who is not hearing , Job 12:3 ; 13:2 מִכֶּם אָנֹכִי נֹפֵל לֹא , Zeph 3:5 (very anomalous); 1Kin 10:21 לא is probably textual error In לוֺ שׂנֵא לֹא וְהוּא or לו הוא שׂנא לא , Deut 4:42 ; 19:4 , 6 ; Josh 20:5 (compare אֹיֵב Num 35:23 ), שׂנֵא is best construed as a substantive, he being a not-hater to him afore-time. — In most of the cases under b, c , אין could have been employed; but the negation by לֹא is more pointed and forcible. 2 Not in predication: a. coupled to an adjective to negative it, like the Greek ἀ- , but usually by way of litotes: Hosea 13:13 לאחֿכם בן an unwise son, Psa 36:5 טוֺב לֹא דֶּרֶךְ a way not good , 43:1 חסיד לא גוי , Prov 16:29 ; 30:25-26 , Ezek 20:25 ; 2Chr 30:17 : Isa 16:14 כַבִּיר לוֺא , compare 10:7 מְעַט לֹא . b. with a participle Jer 2:2 זרועה לא ארץ , 18:15 (the finite verb is more common: see Isa 62:12 נֱעֶזָ֫בָה לֹא עִיר (compare 54:11 ), Jer 6:8 נוֺשָׁ֫בָה לוֺא אֶרֶץ , 15:18 ; 22:6 ; 31:18 ; Zeph 2:1 ). c. Gen 15:13 להם לא בארץ , Jer 5:19 ; Hab 1:6 לֹאלֿוֺ מִשְׁכָּנוֺת , Prov 26:17 לֹאלֿוֺ רִיב . d. with a substantive, in poetry, forming a kind of compound, expressing pointedly its antithesis or negation (German un- is sometimes used similarly): Deut 32:5 (?). 17. 21 a they made me jealous אֵל בְּלֹא with a not-God (with what in no respect deserved the name of God), v b עָם בְּלֹא i.e. with an unorganized horde, Amos 6:13 דָבָר לְלֹא הַשְּׂמֵחִים i.e. at a thing which is not , an unreality (of their boasted strength), Isa 10:15 עֵץ לֹא מַטֶּה כְּהָרִים like a rod's lifting up what is no wood (but the agent wielding it), 31:8 אדם לא חרב אישׁ, לא חרב , 55:2 לחם בלוא for what is not bread , לשׂבעה בלוא for what is not for satiety, Jer 5:7 אֱלֹהִים בְּלֹא וַיּשָּֽׁבְעוּ by not-gods , in late prose 2Chr 13:9 אֱלֹהִים לְלֹא כֹּהֵן ; Psa 44:13 בְּלֹאהֿוֺן עַמְּךָ תִּמְכֹּר for no-value (i.e. cheaply), Prov 13:23 ; Job 10:12 סְדָרִים וְלֹא צלמות darkness and disorder ; so לֹאעַֿמִּי Hosea 1:9 ; Hosea 2:25: still more pregnantly Job 26:2 a לְלֹאכֹֿחַ מֶהעָֿזַרְתָּ (poetic for כח לו אין לאשׁר ) the powerless , 26:2 b; 26:3 a (Ew § 286 g Ges § 152 . 1 n.), 39:16 לָהּ לְלֹא בָּנֶיהָ הִקְשִׁיחַ useth hardly her young ones (making them) into none of hers ; and even Hab 2:6 לֹאלֿוֺ הַמַּרְבֶּה what is not his own (compare Job 18:15 לוֺ מִבְּלִי ). compare with a verb, and ellipse of אשׁר , Isa 65:1 שָׁאָ֑לוּ לְלֹא to those who have not asked, v b Jer 2:8 יוֺעִילוּ לֹא אַחֲרִי , 2:11 b; also רֻחָ֫מָה לֹא Hosea 1:6 , 8 ; Hosea 2:25, and probably Job 31:31 נִשְׂבָּ֑ע לֹא (perfect in p.) one not satisfied. e. in circumstantial clauses (Dr § 164 ), in poetry and rare: qualifying a substantive, 2Sam 23:4 עָבוֺת לֹא בֹּקֶר a morning without clouds , Job 12:24 דֶרֶךְ לֹא בְּתֹהוּ in a pathless waste, 38:26 a; and a verb 34:24 חֵקֶר לֹא כַּבִּרִים יָרֹעַ without inquiry , Psa 59:4 חטאתי ולא פשׁעי לא (compare 59:4 עון בלי ), in late prose, twice, 1Chr 2:30 , 32 בנים לא וימת ( אֵין and בְּלִי , q. v., are more usual in such cases). 3 Once (according to many MSS), as a substantive, Job 6:21 לֹא הֱיִיתֶם כִּיעַֿתָּה for now are ye become nothing , Hi De Kö (compare Dan 4:32 (Aramaic) ᵑ7 חֲשִׁיבִין, כְּלָה here הֲוֵיתוּן כְּלָא , and אַל Job 24:25 ); but reading fluctuates (Orientals לֹא , Qr לו , Westerns, Baer (see pp. 37, 56) לוֺ ['now are ye become that ,' namely the אַכְזָב נַחַל of 24:15 ]; but even לוֺ yields a forced sense; and text is probably wrong: Mich Ew Ol Sgf Bu כֵּןלִ֗֗֗י ( ᵑ6 ᵐ5 also read לִי ); Bö Di כִּילְ֗֗֗אָ֑יִן . compare Kö ii. 1. 236 f . 4 With prefixes: — a. בְּלֹא 31 (chiefly in poetry or late), according to the varying significance of בְּ : ( a ) usually with not = without , Jer 22:13 צדק בלאֿ ביתו בונה without justice (|| משׁפט בלא ; so Ezek 22:29 ; Prov 16:8 ), Isa 55:1 (twice in verse); Prov 19:2 ; Job 8:11 בִצָּה בְּלֹא הֲיִגְאֶהגֹּֿמֶא without mire || מים כלי , 30:28 חַמָּה בְּלֹא (=not through the sun), Lam 1:6 בלאכֿח וילכו , Num 35:22 צְדִיָּה בְּלֹא ֗֗֗ אֵיבָה בְּלֹא , 35:23 (followed by infinitive) רְאוֺת בְּלֹא , 2Chr 21:20 ; Eccl 10:11 ; Psa 17:1 מִרְמָה שִׂפְתֵי בְּלֹא תְּפִלָּתִי ; used more freely in Chronicles, 1Chr 12:18 בְּכַמָּֽי׃ חָמָס בְּלֹא , v. 12:34 וָלֵב לֵב בְּלֹא , 2Chr 30:18 כַכָּתוּב בְּלֹא . With ellipse of rel., Lam 4:14 יִגְּעוּ יוּכְלוּ בְּלֹא without (that) men are able to touch, etc. ( b ) of time, in not , i.e. outside of , Lev 15:25 עֶתנִֿדָּתָהּ בלא , before Job 15:32 בלאיֿומו , Eccl 7:17 עִתֶּךְ׃ בְּלֹא . ( c ) where לֹא belongs to the following word, and is only accidentally preceded by ב (see above 2d ), Deut 32:21 (twice in verse); Jer 5:7 ; Prov 13:23 משׁפט בלא through injustice ; with בְּ pretii , Psa 44:13 ; Isa 55:2 (twice in verse); Jer 2:11 יוֺעִיל בְּלוֺא for (that which) profiteth not. b. הֲלֹא nonne ? Gen 4:7 + often Inviting, as it does, an affirmative answer, it is often used, ( a ) especially in conversation, for pointing to a fact in such a way as to arouse the interest of the person addressed, or to win his assent: Genesis 13:19 Is not the whole land before thee ? 19:20 ; 20:5 ; 27:36 ; 29:25 ; Exod 4:11 Who maketh dumb or deaf, etc. Do not I ? 33:16 ; Judg 4:6 , 14 ; 8:2 ; 9:28 , 38 ; 1Sam 9:20-21 , 15:17 etc.; with a verb in 1person, Josh 1:9 צויתיך הלא , Judg 6:14 שׁלחתיך הלא , 1Sam 20:30 ; 2Sam 19:23 ; Ruth 2:9 : similarly in a poetical or rhetorical style, Judg 5:30 שׁלל יחלקו ימצאו הלא , Isa 8:19 ; 10:8-9 , 11 ; 28:25 ; 29:17 ; 40:21 , 23 ; 42:24 ; 43:19 etc., Job 4:6 ; 4:21 ; 7:1 ; 10:10 ; 10:20 , etc. ( β ) it has a tendency to become little more than an affirm. particle, declaring with some rhetorical emphasis what is, or might be, well known: Deut 3:11 עַמּוֺן בְּנֵי בְרַבַּת הִיא הֲלֹה , 11:30 ; 1Sam 21:12 וג דוד ׳זה הלוא (compare 29:3 , 5 ; 2Sam 11:3 ), 23:19 ; 2Sam 26:1; 15:35 ; it is thus nearly = הִנֵּה ( ᵐ5 sometimes represents it by ιδου , as Josh 1:9 ; Judg 6:14 ; Ruth 2:9 ; 2Sam 15:35 ); so especially in the phrase of the compiler of Kings, And the rest of the acts of . . ., כְּתוּבִים (הֵמָּה) הֵם הֲלֹא are they not written in, etc. ? 1Kin 11:41 ; 14:29 + often (with which there interchanges כְּתוּבִים הִנָּם 14:19 ; 2Kin 15:11 , 26 , 31 , which is Generally used by the Chronicles, 2Chr 16:11 ; 20:34 , etc.), Josh 10:13 (compare 2Sam 1:18 הִנֵּה ), 1Kin 8:53 ᵐ5 , Est 10:2 ; Psalm 56:14 (strangely: contr. Psa 116:8 ). — הִנֵּה הֲלֹא Hab 2:13 ; 2Chr 25:26 ( הִנָּם ). — On Judg 14:15 , see הֲ 1 end. c. וָלֹ֕א and not = and if not , 2Sam 13:26 ; 2Kin 5:17 . compare וָּיֵשׁ . d. כְּלוֺא Obadiah 16 היו כלוא והיו , poetic for כאשׁר , as though they had not been. e. לְלֹא without , literally in the condition of no . . . 2Chr 15:3 (compare לְאֵין , also in Chronicles). Elsewhere לא belongs to the following word, Amos 6:13 ; 2Chr 13:9 ; Isa 65:1 (twice in verse); Job 26:2-3 , 39:16 (see above 2d ). Note. — Fifteen times, according to Masora (see De Psalms 100. 3 Fr MM 247 Str Prol. Cr. 84 ), לא is written by error for לוֺ , namely Exod 21:8 ; Lev 11:21 ; 25:30 ; 1Sam 2:3 ; 2Sam 16:18 ; 2Kin 8:10 ; Isa 9:2 ; 63:9 ; Psa 100:3 ; 139:16 ; Job 13:15 ; 41:4 ; Prov 19:7 ; 26:2 ; Ezra 4:2 (always with Qr לוֺ ). The passages must be considered each upon its own merits: in some לוֺ yields a preferable sense; but this is not the case in all. There is the same קרי (rightly) on Isa 49:5 ; 1Chr 11:20 ; but these were not considered to rest upon equal authority, and are hence not reckoned with the fifteen. — In Judg 21:22 (see GFM), 1Sam 13:13 ; 20:14 (twice in verse), and in Job 9:33 יֵשׁ לֹא , read probably לֻא for לֹא . לוֺ (Kt 1Sam 2:16 ; 20:2 ), לוֺא , see לֹא . לָא ( לָה Dan 4:32 ) adverb not (Biblical Hebrew לא ; Aramaic of Têma, Egyptian, etc., לא ; Nerab ל (Lzb 301 Cook G1. 67 ); לָא ᵑ7 ; Syriac ); — not Jer 10:11 ; Dan 2:5 , 9 , 10 , etc.; before a participle (so rarely in Biblical Hebrew, 1b c ), Dan 2:27 , 43 ; 3:16 ; 4:4 ; 4:6 ; 4:15 +, so 4:32 חֲשׁיבִין כְּלָה אַרְעָא וְכָלדָּֿאְרֵי ; are as men not accounted of (so Bev Behrm Marti, compare Isa 53:8 חשׁיבין ולא בסירין ᵑ7 ; > most 'accounted as nothing,' for which no analogy, yet compare Psa 39:6 ᵑ7 ); followed by אִיתַי , see אִיתַי . With infinitive and לְ Dan 6:9 לִהַשְׁנָיָה לָא דִּי which it is not to alter = which is not to be altered (compare 6:16 ), Ezra 6:8 (K § 67, 1 Dr § 202, 2 .; compare Isa 35:6 ᵑ7 , D Aramaic Dialektproben, p. 1 ). With interr. הֲלָא Dan 3:24 ; 4:27 ; 6:13 .

occurrences.englishText: No plant of the field was yet in the earth, and no herb of the field had yet sprung up; for Yahweh God had not caused it to rain on the earth. There was not a man to till the ground,
but you shall not eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil; for in the day that you eat of it, you will surely die.”
Yahweh God said, “It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make him a helper comparable to‡ or, suitable for, or appropriate for. him.”
The man gave names to all livestock, and to the birds of the sky, and to every animal of the field; but for man there was not found a helper comparable to him.
The man and his wife were both naked, and they were not ashamed.
Now the serpent was more subtle than any animal of the field which Yahweh God had made. He said to the woman, “Has God really said, ‘You shall not eat of any tree of the garden’?”
but not the fruit of the tree which is in the middle of the garden. God has said, ‘You shall not eat of it. You shall not touch it, lest you die.’ ”
